scope_summary: Rate-limit config effectiveness, middleware order in Kernel.php, throttle bucket scoping, log levels for auth failures.

P1_sre.title: No structured logging on auth failure paths. LoginController returns 400 JSON on credentials_invalid, kiosk_machine_inactive, kiosk_user_inactive, role_exist, etc. without any Log::warning() / Log::notice() call. Brute-force attempts are visible only via the rate-limiter (which emits Laravel's default ThrottleRequests 429 response). For a single-restaurant V1 a SIEM is not deployed; for V1.0.2 / production hardening this is a gap.
P1_sre.evidence: Greps for 'Log::warning|Log::error|auth.failure|login.failed' in app/Http/Controllers/Auth/ returned ZERO hits.
P1_sre.user_impact: Forensic gap: if an attacker is brute-forcing a real staff email and the per-email lockout absorbs the noise, the only signal is in storage/logs/laravel.log if Laravel internally logs throttle hits (it does not by default). Owner cannot answer 'was account X targeted last week?'
P1_sre.proposed_v1_action: V1.0.2 quick win: 4 lines in LoginController.login() after credentials_invalid -> Log::channel('security')->warning('auth.login.failed', ['email'=>..., 'ip'=>...]) + same in KioskMachineLoginController. New log channel + retention policy in config/logging.php. Backlog-able.

P1_sre.title: TrustProxies::$proxies='*' is correct for the LAN nginx+PHP-FPM topology BUT documented gotcha: if ever fronted by a public load balancer that doesn't strip X-Forwarded-For (e.g. naive cloud setup), an attacker can spoof source IP -> defeats every per-IP rate-limit AND poisons access logs. Wave 3c added TrustHosts as the partial mitigation (host header anchored) BUT $proxies='*' itself is intentionally permissive for the local deploy.
P1_sre.evidence: TrustProxies.php:24 `protected $proxies = '*';` with explicit comment at lines 13-22.
P1_sre.user_impact: Acceptable for V1 single-restaurant on localhost. Risk emerges only on public hosting -- which BRAIN feedback_no_cloud_until_owner_initiates_2026-05-18 confirms is deferred.
P1_sre.proposed_v1_action: None V1. Production-readiness checklist for the day cloud-deploy is greenlit: validate proxy IP allowlist (e.g. AWS ELB private CIDRs) and tighten $proxies to that range.

P2_sre.title: Rate-limit bucket inventory in RouteServiceProvider::configureRateLimiting -- 10 distinct named limiters: api (120/min default), kiosk-orders (5/min), kiosk-menu (60/min), admin-mutation (30 or 120/min for POS), pos-quote (120/min), pos-order-create (60/min), pos-order-update (120/min), kiosk-login (30/min by username|ip), oss-public (60/min IP-only), login-lockout (10 per 10min by email|ip). All keyed correctly with `user?->id ?: ip` or composite keys. login-lockout uses is_string() guard against fuzz array attack (W8.B REM B3) -- defensive.
P2_sre.evidence: RouteServiceProvider.php:50-173. Comment block at :154-173 explicitly defends against email[]=foo array casts.
P2_sre.user_impact: Working, well-documented. Each bucket has rationale comments.
P2_sre.proposed_v1_action: None V1. The /authcheck endpoint at routes/api.php:202 has NO rate-limit -- post-Sanctum it's safe (auth:sanctum is implicit via the outer 'auth' group) but worth a 60/min belt-and-braces. Not a P1.

P2_sre.title: Middleware priority array in Kernel.php:80-95 is locally extended to insert EnsureUserStatusActive AFTER AuthenticatesRequests. Without this explicit override, Laravel's parent default would `array_unshift` an unknown middleware to position 0 -- placing it BEFORE auth resolves and bypassing the gate. This is non-obvious; future Laravel upgrade may shift the parent array and require re-validation.
P2_sre.proposed_v1_action: Add a Sentinel feature test that asserts EnsureUserStatusActive runs after Sanctum's TokenGuard resolves a user (existing tests if any cover this -- not validated by this audit). V1.0.2 task.

P2_sre.title: /api/auth/authcheck (routes/api.php:202-236) returns full user + permission + menu payload. Used on SPA hydration. Public exposure of an authenticated user's role/menu structure is by design (the user needs it). BUT there is NO throttle bucket on this endpoint specifically (it inherits the prefix 'auth' group's apiKey + localization only). A logged-in client could call /authcheck in a tight loop and burn CPU on PermissionResource::collection + MenuService->menu queries.
P2_sre.evidence: routes/api.php:202-236. No ->middleware('throttle:...') chain on the Route::post('/authcheck').
P2_sre.user_impact: Low. Single-restaurant V1. Not exploitable externally without a valid login. Resource exhaustion vector internal-only.

P2_sre.title: Auth uses Sanctum 'sanctum' guard for API, 'web' guard for login transient session (LoginController.php:60 `Auth::guard('web')->attempt` -> :100 `Auth::guard('web')->logout` to close it). The deliberate handshake (open web -> rehash -> revoke prior tokens -> issue PAT -> close web) is correct and well-commented but COMPLEX. Future devs may regress by skipping the logout. Hardcoded by the comment block at LoginController.php:82-86.
P2_sre.proposed_v1_action: None V1. Feature test exists likely. Not validated by this read-only audit.

rate_limit_coverage_matrix.logout_kioskLogout_deleteAccount: INHERIT 'auth:sanctum' group throttle (none explicit). Re-using normal 'api' bucket 120/min via auth:sanctum chain via outer group. ACCEPTABLE.
